_comment: SPIKE HARNESS - E8 verifier-vs-judge. Every value here is pinned and hashed into the harness fingerprint. Do not import from product code. Delete after 2026-11-30.

corpus._scope_note: PREREGISTRATION.md 2 pins the scoring set to the 11 COMPLETE run directories present at 2026-08-03 07:10. Records from 20260803T070942-diag-... or later are out of scope and belong to E9. corpus_freeze.json carries the per-file SHA-256 of every results.jsonl and traces.jsonl in scope; freeze.py refuses to start on any mismatch.

battery._note: tasks.json is read for the task PROMPT only. Its 'check' object is oracle material and is stripped by redact.scoring_view before any prompt is assembled.
battery._expected_note: expected.json is ORACLE MATERIAL and never reaches a scorer. It is read by corpus.eligibility only, to decide whether a record's stored `expected` still agrees with the battery it is about to be joined against (Amendment B3.2). Both files are hashed into corpus_freeze.json; freeze.verify_battery refuses if either moves.

eligibility.rule: PREREGISTRATION.md Amendment B3.2, as corrected by B4
eligibility._rule_note: A record is eligible only if the join between it and today's battery can be attested. Two ways to attest: the run executed today's battery_version (no cross-battery join happens at all), or the record's stored `expected` still equals today's for its task (the answer did not change). A record whose stored `expected` DISAGREES is stale and excluded — that is B3.2 verbatim. A cross-battery record with no `expected` to compare is UNATTESTED: the eligibility question cannot be answered, and answering it 'yes' by default is the exact error that produced this defect.
eligibility._on_unattested_note: B3.2 mandates only the stale exclusion. Excluding the unattested class is this harness's conservative extension, recorded in Amendment B4 with its cost. Set to 'include' to see what the permissive reading buys; both populations are printed either way, so the choice is visible rather than baked in.

scoring_set._seed_note: PREREGISTRATION.md 9.1 requires a seed recorded in the manifest before selection but does not name one. 20260803 (the preregistration's own date) is fixed here, in the committed config, before any selection was run. Changing it after any verdict exists is an amendment.

b_prime.name: cheap-judge-control
b_prime._id_note: PREREGISTRATION.md 10 prices arm (b') at $0.80/M input and $4.00/M output and calls it 'Haiku-class' without naming a snapshot. claude-3-5-haiku-20241022 is the dated snapshot carrying exactly those list prices. Pinned here, before any call, so the arm is not chosen after seeing (b).

judge_prompt._note: Written once, before any judge call, hashed into the manifest, and not tuned per family, per arm, or after any verdict (PREREGISTRATION.md 7.2).

repeats._note: PREREGISTRATION.md 5.3: three independent calls per trace per judge arm at temperature 0. 10's pre-authorised contingency drops POSITIVES ONLY to 2 if the pre-call projection exceeds the trigger. Negatives always keep three; they carry the discriminative signal.

cost._bytes_per_token_note: PREREGISTRATION.md 10 estimates tokens at 4 bytes/token (13,458 bytes -> 3,365 tokens). The same divisor is used here so the projection is comparable to the preregistered arithmetic. It is an estimate, not a tokenizer; the live accumulator bills measured usage from the API response, never the estimate.
cost._contingency_scope_note: PREREGISTRATION.md 10 says 'projects arm (b)'s cost. If the projection exceeds $6.50 ...'. Read literally, arm (b) alone is planned at $3.83 expected / $5.23 pessimistic and the trigger could never fire. The $6.50 trigger sits between the document's own combined judge subtotals ($4.85 expected, $6.62 pessimistic), so 'combined (b)+(b') judge spend' is the only reading under which the contingency is live. That reading is recorded here and both projections are printed. See README.md 'Disagreements'.

gate._discount_source: findings/007-contract-extraction.md validated-extraction rate. PREREGISTRATION.md 6.4: the decision table reads the DISCOUNTED figure.

predicted_null._note: PREREGISTRATION.md 4.6 / 7.5 / S3. c1 is predicted to catch 0 numeric value errors because a wrong float is a well-typed float. Any detection voids c1. preregistered_n is checked against the mechanically classified count and a mismatch is reported loudly as requiring an amendment; it does not silently change the control.

credentials._note: Resolution: the process environment, else a dotenv tree the operator names with --env-root / F2A_ENV_ROOT. No default path, no guessing, exit with a usage message. No credential VALUE is ever read into a log, trace, manifest, error message, or prompt.
